worked_solution:
Let's reverse the limits of integration on the known result:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{\int }_{3}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x=6\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can split up the given integral using the sum rule and factor out the constants. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{3}(8-f(x))\,\text{d}x & =8{\int }_{1}^{3}\text{d}x-{\int }_{1}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =8\cdot x\,{|}_{1}^{3}-6 \\  & =8(3-1)-6 \\  & =8\cdot 2-6 \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$
